1 سَخَلَهُمْ , aor.
سَخَلَ , (K,) inf. n. سَخْلٌ, (TA,) He drove away, repelled, or banished, them: (K, TA: [in the CK, نَقّاهُمْ is erroneously put for نَفَاهُمْ:]) and خَسَِلَهُمْ signifies the same. (TA.) ―
-b2- And سَخَلَ الشَّىْءَ He took the thing by deceit (K, TA) and by seizure: but not known to Az except on the authority of Lth; and its correctness is doubted by him, unless it be formed by transposition from خَلَسَ, like as they said جَذَبَ and جَبَذَ, and بَضَّ and ضَبَّ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
